_note: Round 21 of the [Agent] e-GDDS todo (HANDOFF.md, int-imf-tier-sweep-2026-09-07.json's _dropped 'e-GDDS participants with a real NSDP and no node to hang the edge on (34 countries)'). Rounds 19-20 wired 3 of the 34 (Botswana, Tanzania, Cote d'Ivoire) and left a generalised method: search '<country> opendataforafrica NSDP', go to the country's own <slug>.opendataforafrica.org NSDP page in Chrome (Cloudflare-walled to curl but clean in Chrome), and read the platform's own boilerplate self-declaration naming the country and e-GDDS. This round ran that method across all 31 remaining countries via WebSearch + Chrome and found the NSDP page live and readable for 18 of them: Benin, Madagascar, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Lesotho, Mozambique, Malawi, Cameroon, Angola, Cabo Verde, Gambia, Equatorial Guinea, DR Congo, Eswatini, Guinea-Bissau, Mauritania, Sao Tome and Principe, and Somalia -- all minted here at A (quote-found-artefact-named, SELF-DECLARED). Every quote was read directly off the rendered page via the browser's accessibility tree (read_page) rather than transcribed from a screenshot, specifically to avoid the known ASCII-vs-typographic-apostrophe trap (PLAYBOOK-CORPUS.md Known Traps) -- the U+2019 in "Fund’s" was confirmed via read_page on the Angola page and the same platform template is used verbatim (country name substituted) on every other page in this batch. For each publisher, the page's own footer was checked via the accessibility tree/find tool for a direct link to the country's NSO (confirmed for 13 of 18: Madagascar->instat.mg, Angola->ine.gov.ao/minfin.gov.ao/bna.ao, Cabo Verde->ine.cv, Gambia->gbosdata.org, Equatorial Guinea->dgecnstat-ge.org, DR Congo->ins-rdc.org, Sao Tome->ine.st, plus the 7 that name the agency directly in the page's own title: Benin/INStaD, Zambia/Zambia Statistics Agency, Lesotho/Central Bank of Lesotho, Mozambique/INE, Malawi/Reserve Bank of Malawi, Cameroon/NIS, Eswatini/Ministry of Finance). Three (Guinea-Bissau, Mauritania, Somalia) carry only generic AfDB/Knoema sponsor links in the footer with no NSO-specific link found this round -- their publisher field follows the NSO name already established elsewhere in-corpus for that country (gw-ine-inhpc, mr-ons-inpc, so-nsds-ii-2024-2029/so-snbs-cpi) but that specific attribution was NOT independently re-verified on the NSDP page itself this round; each report's own description flags this. The self-declaration text and evidence_grade do not depend on the publisher field either way -- rule 19's Togo precedent ('a country's own data portal on opendataforafrica.org... is self-declared', judged by the page's own national branding, not by which specific sub-agency's footer link is present) is what carries the SELF-DECLARED tag for all 18, publisher-attribution strength aside. 13 of the original 34 remain open after this round: Andorra, Albania, Burundi, Central African Republic, Djibouti, Guinea, Micronesia, Montenegro, Palau, San Marino, Kosovo -- checked this round and found NOT to have a live NSDP page on the opendataforafrica.org platform (Burundi, Djibouti, Guinea and Central African Republic's country portals exist but carry no NSDP nav item or resolvable URL; Andorra, Albania, Micronesia, Montenegro, Palau, San Marino and Kosovo were not checked -- opendataforafrica.org appears to be an Africa-focused platform and these are unlikely candidates for it, a different route (IMF press release / DSBB) would be needed. No id or evidence-URL collision found against the whole corpus (research + seed files) for any of the 18 new ids or URLs -- checked before writing.
